literal: " When old he was much swayed by his wife Lady Meng and for this was mocked.
idiomatic: " In old age he was much ruled by his wife Lady Meng and was ridiculed for it.

literal: He and his cousin Song both held the Three Excellencies—a glory of the age.
idiomatic: He and his cousin Song both reached the Three Excellencies—the glory of their day.

literal: His son Xian held office as Vice Minister; he died young.
idiomatic: His son Xian was Vice Minister and died young.

literal: Xian's son Guan in youth was famed for bold courage; later he inherited his grandfather's title as Prince of Shangdang.
idiomatic: Xian's son Guan was famed in youth for courage; later he inherited the title Prince of Shangdang.

literal: At that time alien surnames inheriting titles were mostly reduced to duke; the emperor because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding court in an earlier reign specially did not reduce him.
idiomatic: Alien princes were usually demoted to duke; because his grandfather Daosheng had aided the founding reign, the emperor did not demote him.

literal: As General Who Pacifies the West and Acting Minister of Works he supervised military affairs of the seven western garrisons in a campaign against Tuyuhun.
idiomatic: As General Who Pacifies the West and Acting Minister of Works he commanded the seven western garrisons against Tuyuhun.

literal: The tribal chief Shiyin fled and hid, burning the cities he had held before returning.
idiomatic: Chief Shiyin fled and hid, burning his cities before withdrawing.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaowen he was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: At Xiaowen's accession he was Director of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant.

literal: When Tuyuhun again pressed the border, he was again lent the Acting Ministry of Works to campaign and subdue them.
idiomatic: When Tuyuhun invaded again he was again lent the seal of Acting Minister of Works to subdue them.

literal: Later he was General Who Pacifies the South.
idiomatic: Later he was General Who Pacifies the South.

literal: He died; his posthumous name was Ding.
idiomatic: He died; his posthumous name was Ding.

literal: His funeral followed the precedent of his grandfather the Tranquil Prince and he was buried at the Clouds-in-the-Middle Golden Tomb.
idiomatic: His funeral followed his grandfather the Tranquil Prince and he was buried at the Golden Tomb in Yunzhong.

literal: Great-grandson You
idiomatic: Great-grandson You

literal: His son Jigui at six inherited the title and was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: His son Jigui at six inherited the title and was demoted to duke.

literal: Xiaowen because he bore the family charge while young bestowed the name You, style Chengye.
idiomatic: Xiaowen, seeing him bear the house while still young, gave him the name You, styled Chengye.

literal: Chengye was clever and talented, humble and fond of scholars; as Forward General he followed Xiaowen on the southern campaign.
idiomatic: Chengye was clever, talented, humble, and loved scholars; as Forward General he followed Xiaowen south.

literal: In Emperor Xuanwu's time he was Governor of Yang Province, Acting General Who Guards the South, and commander of Huainan military affairs.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was Governor of Yang, Acting General Who Guards the South, and commander of Huainan.

literal: The Liang generals Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized Shouchun; Chengye's sons were fierce and Sui found them hard to face, calling them the "little irons."
idiomatic: Liang's Pei Sui and Yu Hong seized Shouchun; Chengye's sons were ferocious and Sui called them the "little irons."

literal: An edict had the Prince of Hejian lead the host to relieve them.
idiomatic: An edict ordered the Prince of Hejian to lead reinforcements.

literal: The prince wished to give battle; Chengye because rain had lasted long urged greater caution.
idiomatic: The prince wanted battle; Chengye, with rains prolonged, urged patience.

literal: The prince would not listen and gave battle; the enemy seized the chance; Chengye brought up the rear.
idiomatic: The prince refused, fought, was exploited by the foe; Chengye covered the retreat.

literal: At first, because Chengye held strong troops and long refused battle, critics suspected other designs.
idiomatic: At first, since Chengye held a strong host and would not fight, some suspected ulterior motives.

literal: The court again sent the Prince of Hejian, the Prince of Huaiyang Yu, and Director of the Masters of Writing Li Xian as three commanders—in name to aid Chengye, in fact to guard against him.
idiomatic: The court sent the Prince of Hejian, Prince of Huaiyang Yu, and Li Xian as three commanders—ostensibly to help Chengye, in truth to watch him.

literal: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Zhongshan, Chengye was made Grand Commander for the Northern Campaign.
idiomatic: When Xianyu Xiuli rebelled at Zhongshan, Chengye was made Grand Commander of the Northern Expedition.

literal: Soon, reaching Ye as chief envoy, an edict relieved Chengye of the mobile secretariat, removed his grand envoy status, and sent the Prince of Hejian as Grand Commander and Li Daoyuan as mobile secretariat.
idiomatic: Soon, reaching Ye as chief envoy, an edict stripped him of the mobile secretariat and grand envoy rank and made the Prince of Hejian Grand Commander with Li Daoyuan as secretariat.

literal: Chengye sent his son Ziyu with a memorial saying he and the prince were together in Huainan and both faced the state's peril.
idiomatic: Chengye sent his son Ziyu with a memorial: he and the prince were both in Huainan facing national crisis.

literal: The prince was defeated while he remained whole, and private rancor arose.
idiomatic: The prince was beaten while he stayed intact, and private bitterness grew.

literal: Moreover, seizing command on the eve of battle was not his strength.
idiomatic: Moreover, snatching command at the critical hour was no skill of his.

literal: The memorial was not accepted.
idiomatic: The memorial was rejected.

literal: The prince and Chengye advanced to Hulu; Chengye did not wish to fight and the prince would not listen.
idiomatic: Prince and Chengye reached Hulu; Chengye would not fight and the prince would not heed him.

literal: Marching to Wulu they were ambushed by Xiuli; the prince would not go to their aid; the rebels gathered and they were utterly defeated.
idiomatic: At Wulu, Xiuli ambushed them; the prince would not aid; rebels massed and they were routed.

literal: Chengye and the prince were both struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: Chengye and the prince were both removed from office.

literal: Soon the commandery of Zhengping in Shu rebelled; Chengye was again lent General Who Pacifies the West and Commander for the Shu Campaign.
idiomatic: Soon Zhengping in Shu rebelled; Chengye was again lent General Who Pacifies the West and Commander against Shu.

literal: Repeated battles brought merit; he was made General Who Pacifies the East and his original title restored.
idiomatic: Repeated victories won him General Who Pacifies the East and restoration of his title.

literal: Later he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he was Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Before long, Governor of Yong Province Xiao Baoyin held the province in rebellion; Chengye was again made mobile secretariat to attack him.
idiomatic: Soon Yong Governor Xiao Baoyin rebelled; Chengye was again mobile secretariat against him.

literal: Chengye's back abscess had not healed; Empress Dowager Ling comforted him, "Your ailment runs so deep; I wished to rest you, yet there is no other to entrust—what can be done?"
idiomatic: Chengye's back sore was unhealed; Empress Dowager Ling said, "Your wound is so grave I wished to let you rest, yet none else can be trusted—what is to be done?"

literal: Chengye answered, "After death one stops—how dare I not exert myself?"
idiomatic: Chengye answered, "I serve until death—how dare I not strive?"

literal: At that time his son Yan also had foot sores; leaning on a staff he came to take leave.
idiomatic: His son Yan had foot sores too; leaning on a staff he came to bid farewell.

literal: Vice Director Yuan Shun looked at his peers and said, "We are prepared as great ministers, each in favor—on a day of peril should the sick go first? Is that not wrong!"
idiomatic: Vice Director Yuan Shun said to his fellows, "We stand as chief ministers in favor—on a day of danger must the sick lead the way? Can that be right?"

literal: None replied.
idiomatic: No one answered.

literal: At that time Xue Fengxian rebelled in Zhengping and Xue Xiuyi gathered forces in Hedong, seizing the salt pools and besieging Puban, east and west linking to answer Baoyin.
idiomatic: Xue Fengxian rebelled in Zhengping; Xue Xiuyi massed in Hedong, seized the salt pools, besieged Puban, and linked east and west with Baoyin.

literal: Chengye then held Hedong.
idiomatic: Chengye held Hedong.

literal: There was an edict abolishing the salt-pool tax; Chengye memorialized, "The salt pools are Heaven's gift of wealth, close to the capital—only treasure and guard them and share out by rule.
idiomatic: An edict abolished the salt tax; Chengye memorialized: "The salt pools are Heaven's wealth, hard by the capital—they must be treasured, guarded, and fairly shared.

literal: Now on four sides there are many alarms and the treasury is empty; yet Ji and Ding provinces are perishing in disorder and their regular silk levies can no longer be collected.
idiomatic: Now alarms ring on every side and the treasury is bare; Ji and Ding are dying in chaos and their silk dues cannot be gathered.

literal: Looking up at the storehouses, outflow without inflow—balance must be managed, out and in must aid each other.
idiomatic: The coffers spend without receiving—accounts must be balanced, outgo matched by income.

literal: Roughly speaking, in one year the salt tax, measured in silk, should not fall short of three hundred thousand bolts.
idiomatic: In one year the salt levy, reckoned in silk, should not fall below three hundred thousand bolts.

literal: That is like placing Ji and Ding within the capital domain; to abolish it now is to lose twice over.
idiomatic: That is like keeping Ji and Ding within the royal domain; to abolish it now is double loss.

literal: Your servant earlier disobeyed the stern order and did not first attack the border rebels but went straight to relieve Hedong—not because he cared little for Chang'an and hurried to Puban.
idiomatic: I earlier defied the stern order and did not strike the border rebels first but relieved Hedong—not because I slighted Chang'an and rushed to Puban.

literal: Once Puban fell the salt pools would be lost and the three armies' mouths would have no provision—the means of crossing would be cut off.
idiomatic: Once Puban fell the salt pools were lost and the armies' mouths had no supply—the lifeline was cut.

literal: Heaven aided Great Wei and this plan did not miss.
idiomatic: Heaven aided Great Wei and the plan held.

literal: In Gaozu's years of peace there was no lack, yet he still created salt officials and added guardians.
idiomatic: Even in Gaozu's peaceful years, when want was unknown, he set salt officers and guardians.

literal: It was not for goods to compete for profit but fearing that from profit custom would be corrupted.
idiomatic: Not to wring profit from goods but lest profit corrupt custom.

literal: Moreover today princes and dukes eat salary without service and officials hold post without work; rent is levied for six years' grain and corvée mulcts next year's resources.
idiomatic: Today lords feast without serving and officers draw pay without labor; rent takes six years' grain and corvée eats next year's stock.

literal: All this is private outlay seizing men's strength—not what we wish, but what we cannot avoid.
idiomatic: All is private spending of public muscle—not our wish but our bind.

literal: Your servant has ordered the supervising office and the commandant to return with their commands and resume regular collection, awaiting further edict.
idiomatic: I have ordered the supervising office and commandant to return with their troops and collect the tax as usual, pending further command.

literal: " When Yong Province was pacified he was made Governor of Yong.
idiomatic: " When Yong was pacified he was made its governor.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang he was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang, soon changed to Prince of Fengyi, later reduced to Commandery Duke.
idiomatic: At Xiaozhuang's accession he was Prince of Shangdang, soon Prince of Fengyi, later demoted to commandery duke.

literal: He was transferred to Duke of the Ministry of Works, added Palace Attendant, Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Secretariat, and still garrisoned Chang'an.
idiomatic: He became Duke of Works, Palace Attendant, Concurrent Director and Grand Secretariat, still holding Chang'an.

literal: When Jiemin was enthroned he was transferred to Duke of the Grand Commandant and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: When Jiemin succeeded he was Grand Commandant and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing.

literal: After defeat at Hanling, Husijun first held Heyang Bridge and plotted to kill Erzhu.
idiomatic: After defeat at Hanling, Husijun seized Heyang Bridge and plotted to kill the Erzhu clan.

literal: Chengye was sent into Luoyang to inform Jiemin of the intent to execute Shilong and his brothers.
idiomatic: Chengye was sent to Luoyang to tell Jiemin of the plan to kill Shilong and his brothers.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu he was transferred to Grand Tutor; for settling the succession he was further enfeoffed Baron of the Opening State.
idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession he was Grand Tutor; for fixing the succession he was further enfeoffed Baron of the Opening State.

literal: Chengye memorialized asking that the enfeoffment be transferred to his maternal cousin's son, the Vice Director of the Court for Ceremonials Yuan Hongchao's second son Yun.
idiomatic: He asked to transfer the enfeoffment to his cousin's son Yun, second son of Vice Director Yuan Hongchao.

literal: At first Chengye's mother died at his birth and he was raised by Hongchao's mother; hence the request to yield.
idiomatic: His mother died at his birth; Hongchao's mother raised him—hence the request.

literal: It was granted.
idiomatic: It was granted.

literal: When Emperor Wu entered the passes Chengye was then garrisoning Wulao; he also followed to Chang'an, held office as Grand Preceptor and recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing, and was enfeoffed Prince of Shangdang.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu entered the passes Chengye held Wulao and followed to Chang'an as Grand Preceptor, recording affairs, and Prince of Shangdang.

literal: In the first year of Datong he died; he was posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Chancellor, commander of thirty provinces' military affairs and Governor of Yong, posthumous name Wensuan.
idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he died, posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Chancellor, commander of thirty provinces and Governor of Yong, posthumous name Wensuan.

literal: In youth Chengye was light and chivalrous, cockfighting and racing horses, striving in killings; he fled and reached the house of Chen Xingde, garrison commander at Longmen.
idiomatic: In youth Chengye was rakish—cockfights, horses, brawls that killed—and fled to Longmen garrison commander Chen Xingde.

literal: When an amnesty came he was spared.
idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

literal: He therefore gave his stepwife Luo's daughter by her former husband, the Lü clan, in marriage to Xingde's elder brother Xingen in return.
idiomatic: He married his stepmother Luo's stepdaughter, a Lü, to Xingde's brother Xingen in gratitude.

literal: Luo was more than ten years older than Chengye and fiercely jealous.
idiomatic: Luo was more than ten years Chengye's senior and fiercely jealous.

literal: Chengye still respected and loved her deeply and kept no concubines.
idiomatic: Chengye still honored and loved her and kept no concubines.

literal: Among boy attendants at Chengye's side, those suspected and put to death numbered several.
idiomatic: Several boy attendants at his side were suspected and killed.

literal: His first wife Lady Zhang had two sons, Ziyan and Ziyu.
idiomatic: His first wife Lady Zhang bore Ziyan and Ziyu.

literal: Luo bore three sons: Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang.
idiomatic: Luo bore Shaoyuan, Shiliang, and Jiliang.

literal: The brothers were all bold in war.
idiomatic: The brothers were all fierce in battle.

literal: Ziyan's original name was Jun; he had great strength and for repeated service in his father's campaigns was enfeoffed Baron of Huaili.
idiomatic: Ziyan, originally Jun, was immensely strong; for repeated campaigns with his father he was Baron of Huaili.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu fell out with Qi Shenwu, Ziyan was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and Vice Director of the Secretariat, garrisoning Hengnong as his trusted arm.
idiomatic: When Xiaowu quarreled with Qi Shenwu, Ziyan was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and Vice Director, garrisoning Hengnong as his right hand.

literal: When he followed the emperor into the passes he was enfeoffed Duke of Gaoping and made Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.
idiomatic: Following the emperor into the passes he was Duke of Gaoping and Equal in Rank to Three Ministers.

literal: For following the campaign against Dou Tai and fighting at Shayuan he was made Opening Office and Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: For campaigning against Dou Tai and fighting at Shayuan he was made Opening Office and Palace Attendant.

literal: When the east was recovered and the old capital restored, Ziyan was made Concurrent Director of the Masters of Writing and Acting Governor of Si Province, remaining to garrison Luoyang.
idiomatic: When the east was recovered he was Concurrent Director and Acting Governor of Si, left to hold Luoyang.

literal: Later, because things went ill, the army withdrew.
idiomatic: Later, when affairs turned bad, the army withdrew.

literal: In the seventh year of Datong he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of Datong he was Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

literal: Ziyan in youth had often fallen from his horse and broken his arm; the bone above the elbow rose more than an inch.
idiomatic: In youth Ziyan often fell and broke his arm; bone rose an inch above the elbow.

literal: He then ordered the flesh cut open and the bone sawed; blood flowed in several sheng and he spoke as if in jest.
idiomatic: He had the flesh opened and the bone sawed; blood poured in sheng yet he jested calmly.

literal: Men of the time thought him beyond Guan Yu.
idiomatic: His age thought him bolder than Guan Yu.

literal: In his last years stone eruptions broke out over his body; even kin thought it a foul disease.
idiomatic: In his last years stony growths broke out; kin took it for a foul disease.

literal: Ziyan said, "With a foul disease like this it is hard to prove oneself innocent.
idiomatic: Ziyan said, "With such a disease I cannot prove my innocence.

literal: There is no good physician in the world—I am as good as dead!
idiomatic: There is no skilled doctor in the world—I am as good as dead!

literal: I have heard that with foul disease a viper's sting does not hurt—let us try to find one so my brothers may know me.
idiomatic: I have heard that with this disease a viper's bite does not hurt—let us find one so my brothers know I am myself.

literal: " When they got a snake on South Mountain he touched it to his thigh; he cried out in pain and soon the swelling died.
idiomatic: " They found a snake on South Mountain; he touched it to his thigh, cried in pain, and the swelling soon subsided.

literal: When Emperor Wen heard of it.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of it.

literal: He mourned and said, "I have lost my good general!
idiomatic: He wept and said, "I have lost my fine general!

literal: " He was posthumously made Governor of Yong.
idiomatic: " He was posthumously made Governor of Yong.

literal: Ziyu held office as Vice Director of the Imperial Guards.
idiomatic: Ziyu was Vice Director of the Imperial Guards.

literal: He memorialized giving up seventeen ordinary ranks of salary to seek office for his son Yizhen.
idiomatic: He gave up seventeen ranks of ordinary salary to seek office for his son Yizhen.

literal: Yizhen was made Left General and added Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: Yizhen was made Left General and Regular Attendant and Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: Again for his father's merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Pingyuan.
idiomatic: For his father's merit he was also Baron of Pingyuan.

literal: Yizhen's younger brother Si, style name Ruohan.
idiomatic: Yizhen's younger brother Si, styled Ruohan.
